name: Monash University
overview:
IMPORTANT: Additional Program Requirements


Students must have at least a 850 Tepitech score at the moment of the International Jury in order to be considered for this program.


Monash University was established in Melbourne, Australia in 1958.

It is Australia’s largest university with a total enrolment of 83,560 students, from which 27,403 are international students (based on 2018 full-year data).

Monash University is a member of Australia’s prestigious Group of Eight universities and is regularly ranked as one of the top universities in Australia, Asia, and the world.

Monash was ranked 84th best university in the world by The Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2019.

Monash offers a huge range of study options divided in 10 faculties across:

  • Five campuses in Australia
  • A campus in Malaysia
  • A study centre in Prato, Italy

Click here to have more information on the host country. The travaler's advice is issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

Epitech international mobility coordinator will nominate you and create your application session for you on my.application, the online portal for students.

You will then have to complete and submit your application via this portal.

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Application form completed
  • Passport copy
  • Tepitech score certificate: minimum required 850 – ask the administrative assistant of your campus to send it to you
  • Transcripts in English: will be provided directly to the university by the IAFF team on my.application. Do not upload it yourself.

Later in the process, you will be required to create a study plan.

Your study plan is the list of units (or classes) you plan to study while on exchange/study abroad, and forms part of your application.

This is a key element on which Monash University emphasizes. You can be asked to justify your choices or show your capabilities.

After you apply, your application form will be assessed by Monash Abroad and the relevant faculties.

Follow the link to find out more about our approval process.

To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.

This information is subject to change by the partner university.

They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Reception of the letter of admission

Once your application has been accepted, you will receive your acceptance letter from Monash University.

The letter of acceptance is required by the Australian Immigration Office to proceed with your visa application.


3. Visa

When you receive your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), you can apply for a student visa (subclass 500), Non-Award Sector.

It is your responsibility to get your visa in a timely manner and to understand fully your obligations and responsibilities when applying for a student visa.

Students are advised not to book a non-refundable travel ticket until their visa has been issued.

https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500#Overview

The cost for this visa is AU$ 2000 (2025)


4. Insurance & Health

The mandatory Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is insurance to assist international students in meeting the costs of medical and hospital care that they may need while in Australia.

OSHC will also pay limited benefits for pharmaceuticals and ambulance services.

It is a condition of student visas that visa-length OSHC be purchased and maintained for the duration of that visa.

Failure to purchase OSHC will result in students being non-compliant with their student visa requirements.

Students will be required to purchase OSHC when accepting their offer for Exchange or Study Abroad.

More information will be provided with the offer.

The yearly cost for the OSHC is approximately AU$ 762.

We boldly encourage students to take out comprehensive travel insurance before they leave for Australia, as their OSHC will provide only basic medical and hospital cover whilst in Australia and does not cover any travel-related claims. The OSHC does not cover students while travelling to or from Australia, their personal belongings, or if they have an emergency and need to return home urgently.

All exchange students coming to Monash must have health insurance as required by the respective governments. Health insurance is organised by Monash, so please do not apply online.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform:

https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

For more information, please check the country's health forms here: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/australie
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation:

Living in the halls of residence gives you the chance to become immersed in campus life at Monash and get to know local students. Monash Residential Services runs the halls of residence. Please check their website for more information.

Exchange students are given priority when applying for accommodation at the Clayton campus. Make sure you apply as early as possible as accommodation is not guaranteed to all students that apply.

There are two types:

  • the traditional dorms (Clayton residential village) with common areas (kitchen, bathrooms). All room types are single occupancy only. Prices: 353.15-426.65$/week depending on refurbishment and private bathroom (2026 prices) to live in the halls of residence; 342-353$/week for shared flats. A former student from Epitech chose this option in 2022-2023.
  • the studio apartments (Clayton urban community). Prices: 378-420$/week (2026 prices).

Monash Residential Services makes life in the halls fun with tons of social events and activities for you participate in. You can also take advantage of free TV, internet and Foxtel (pay-tv), and support programs. You may need to buy your own kitchen utensils and bedding.

Most Study Abroad and Exchange students apply to live on the Clayton campus, as availability at the other Australian campuses is limited. Clayton is 20km from the Melbourne CBD and provides lots of options for housing.

Off-campus accommodation:

Monash has a list of preferred off-campus accommodation providers which include:

  • Mannix College - 50 metres from the Clayton campus
  • Iglu South Yarra - 20km from the Clayton campus

Some other options that you could consider when looking for student and share accommodation include:

  • FlatmateFinders
  • Student Housing Australia
courses:
Credits

You will have to validate 48 credits at Monash University over the year; i.e. 24 per semester to validate 60 ECTS.


Academic calendar

The language of instruction at Monash is English. Classes start at the end of July for the fall semester and at the beginning of March for the spring semester. We recommend you arrive in Australia at the beginning of July (especially for students with an on-campus residence) to be able to participate to the orientation week in mid-July.


Fall Semester/Semester 2 at Monash (2026)

  • Orientation: 20-24 Jul
  • Semester 2 teaching period: 27 Jul-18 Nov
  • Mid-semester break: 28 Sep-2 Oct
  • Exams: 2-18 Nov

Spring Semester/Semester 1 at Monash (2026)

  • Orientation: 23-27 Feb
  • Semester 1 teaching period: 2 Mar-26 Jun
  • Mid semester break: 6-10 Apr
  • Exams: 8-26 Jun


Department and courses

EPITECH’s students will be studying at the Faculty of Information Technology, taking 3rd year undergraduate units (courses). Most of the units will take place at the Clayton Campus.

Please refer to the list below for the units’ information (this list is subject to changes depending on unit’s availability):

  • Semester 2 = Fall semester
  • Semester 1 = Spring semester

Courses are subject to change every year but some examples that are possible:

  • Introduction to computer systems, networks and security
  • Introduction to programming (advanced)
  • Mobile application development
  • Usability
  • Software security
  • Computer architecture
  • IT strategy and governance
  • Software engineering: architecture and design
  • Parallel computing
  • Fundamentals of Algorithms
  • Databases
  • Modelling for data analysis
  • Business Intelligence and Data Warehouse
  • Data Analytics
  • Advanced Database Design
  • Leadership principles and practices - MGX3991 Caulfied Campus, Semester 2 (July to November)
  • Introduction to management - MGC1010 Clayton Campus, both semesters
  • IT Strategy and Governance - FIT3174, available for all study abroad students
  • Interntional Business - MGF2351 Caulfield Campus, both semesters


Course Format and Workload

The courses are probably going to be more theoretical than at Epitech.

Some units are assessed through continuous assessment and others through final exams. Everything is generally indicated in the unit and upon first reading.

Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated in the application guide.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: about 1200€
  • Insurance: 300-600€/year depending on the provider & coverage level
  • Visa: AU$ 2000 (2025)
  • Books and materials: AU$ 845 per year

You should also prepare for your home set-up costs and allow AU$3,000-$5,000 to cover establishment expenses, such as bond payment, advance rent, furniture, and other household items. Some student apartments come fully furnished, but private rental accommodation are rarely furnished. Consider the deposit and one month’s rent paid in advance: AU$ 600–1,000 each.


Estimated weekly budget (source: Monash University, 2025)

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

You can also use this cost of living calculator in Australia.

Overall, a single international student requires approximately $30,000 – $45,000 for living expenses per year.

  • Housing

On campus: $330 to $399 per week

Shared rentals: $275 to $380 per week (Clayton area)

Homestay: $275 to $430 per week

Rental: $500 to $750 per week (Clayton area)

  • Other living expenses

Groceries and eating out: $150 to $500 per week

Gas, water and electricity: $40 to $80 per week

Phone and internet: $20 to $46 per week

Public transport: $25 to $50 per week

Car (after purchase): $150 to $300 per week

Entertainment: $150 to $300 per week

These prices are indicative and may vary.


For more information on the cost of living in Melbourne, click here: https://www.monash.edu/students/support/international/before-leaving/expenses-budgeting
